supporting_observations.claim: The provided records do not show a PowerShell process or command line on WS-MLOPEZ-01 at the reported time. Process-creation records included for later in the window identify SearchProtocolHost.exe, GoogleDriveFS.exe, conhost.exe, and WmiPrvSE.exe, not PowerShell.

At 13:37:34, WS-MLOPEZ-01 established an SMB connection to DC-HD-01 and the DC recorded a network logon for the workstation account. These records do not identify a share, command, or PowerShell activity.
At 13:38:45 and 13:39:31, the DC issued service tickets for FILE-HD-01$ to the WS-MLOPEZ-01$ account; the records do not establish what activity, if any, used those tickets.

At 13:44, the proxy recorded a Windows Update Agent tunnel to download.windowsupdate.com transferring about 38.8 MB from the server to the workstation. This is consistent with update activity, but it occurs after the reported approximate time and does not establish that it caused the reported PowerShell window.

A short-lived SYSTEM conhost.exe process was created at 14:12 with csrss.exe as its parent and exited roughly two seconds later. This is later than the reported activity and the records do not link it to the reported window.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not include a PowerShell process-creation event, command line, script-block log, or console transcript for the reported activity; the absence in this evidence does not establish that no PowerShell window appeared.

The supplied records show some workstation process creation later in the review window, but do not provide a complete process timeline for the reported time around 13:40 UTC (for example, T024-00276 and T024-00285).

The SMB and Kerberos records identify connections or tickets, but do not show the accessed share contents, executed commands, or the process responsible for the activity (T024-00053, T024-00057, T024-00067, T024-00072).
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell actually ran on WS-MLOPEZ-01 around 13:40 UTC, and if so, its command line, script, parent process, and user context.
Whether the activity was authorized workstation patching by omar.haddad or another benign action.
Whether the FILE-HD-01$ service tickets or earlier SMB activity were related to the reported window.
Whether any code or payload was downloaded or executed as part of the reported activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect endpoint process and process-tree telemetry for WS-MLOPEZ-01 covering at least 13:20–14:20 UTC, including PowerShell, cmd.exe, conhost.exe, parent processes, command lines, and user/logon context.
Collect PowerShell Operational logs, script-block/module logging, transcripts, and relevant console or EDR telemetry for the same period.
Verify whether omar.haddad performed scheduled workstation patching, and obtain the corresponding remote-session, deployment-script, and FILE-HD-01 share-access records.
Obtain the underlying SMB share-access or file-audit records for the workstation's SMB connections and investigate whether any files or commands were accessed or executed.
unrelated_findings: Google Drive File Stream ran under maria.lopez on WS-MLOPEZ-01 at 14:11 and contacted dl.google.com; Google Drive is not listed among approved services in the supplied environment context. Track separately; this does not establish a link to the reported PowerShell window (T024-00278, T024-00280, T024-00281).

At 14:11–14:12, svchost.exe opened handles to lsass.exe with access values 0x1000 and 0x1400. The records do not identify the service or purpose; review separately without treating this as evidence for the alert (T024-00283, T024-00284, T024-00289).
